q-123191.html:
Question 1
?

Given that r(t)=⟨2t−5,4t+24t⟩, calculate r(6).

a
⟨12,6⟩
b
⟨6,4⟩
c
⟨5,8⟩
d
⟨7,6⟩
e
⟨7,8⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We substitute t=6 into our function, and we get

r(6)=⟨2⋅6−5,4⋅6+246⟩=⟨7,8⟩.

q-50359.name: Question 2
q-50359.worked_solution:
We substitute $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ into our function, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2},\,{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

q-348677.name: Question 3
q-348677.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=3$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(3) & =⟨{log}_{5}⁡({3}^{2}+16),\,tan\,(\frac{3\pi }{9}),\,{3}^{3}-6(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨{log}_{5}⁡(25),\,tan\,(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,27-18⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,\sqrt{3},\,9⟩\end{aligned}
$$

q-160769.name: Question 4
q-160769.problem:
What is the value of 
 $f(s)=\operatorname{tan}⁡s\,i+\operatorname{cot}⁡s\,j-\,k$ at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}?$
q-160769.worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}$  into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,i+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,j-k \\  & =1\,i+1\,j-k \\  & =i+j-k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the value of  $f(s)$ at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}$  is $i+j-k.$

q-160769.html:
Question 4
?

What is the value of f(s)=tan⁡si+cot⁡sj−k at s=π4?

a
−i−j+k
b
−i−j−k
c
i+j−k
d
i+j+k
e
i−j+k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To evaluate, we substitute at s=π4 into the function, as follows:

f(π4)=tan⁡(π4)i+cot⁡(π4)j−k=1i+1j−k=i+j−k

So, the value of f(s) at s=π4 is i+j−k.

q-348693.name: Question 5
q-348693.worked_solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ),\,\sqrt{4},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(1)| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-348690.name: Question 6
q-348690.worked_solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =⟨cos\,(\frac{2\pi }{2}),\,\sqrt{{2}^{3}-4},\,ln\,(2\,{e}^{0}-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ),\,\sqrt{4},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(2)| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4+0} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
